items.title: Do You Neglect Your Salvation?
items.summary: Being a Christian is a very serious business, though not a sour business. We are simply blood-earnest about being happy in our great salvation.

items.title: The Real Problem with Anxiety
items.summary: What you thought was a mere struggle with an anxious disposition might really be a far deeper struggle with trusting God.

items.title: The Meaning of Suffering
items.summary: It is truer in suffering than anywhere else that God is most glorified in us when we are most satisfied in him.

items.title: Rejoicing in Pain
items.summary: Whether we focus on the riches of the reward or the refining effects of suffering, God’s purpose is that our joy in suffering be sustained.

items.title: Christ’s Sufferings in Us
items.summary: We exhibit the sufferings of Christ when we ourselves suffer for those we are trying to win.

items.title: The Seminary of Suffering
items.summary: God designs suffering not only as a way to wean Christians off of self and onto grace, but also as a way to spotlight that grace and make it shine.

items.title: The Danger of Drifting
items.summary: Be satisfied in Jesus so that you do not get lured downstream by deceitful desires.

items.title: How Evil Works
items.summary: How does Satan influence the world, and where do we see his work most clearly? Pastor John describes Satan’s power and limits under Christ’s victorious work.

items.title: Peace for Second-Guessers
items.summary: How do we know when we’ve worked hard enough? Pastor John offers six ways to fight anxiety and rest in the grace of Christ.

items.title: Was Piper Unprepared?
items.summary: In 1980, Bethlehem Baptist Church hired 34-year-old John Piper as lead pastor. Pastor John reflects on the life experience and biblical worldview that prepared him for ministry.

items.title: Happiness Myths to Avoid
items.summary: Modern psychology defines happiness as “self-fulfillment.” But without God, our souls will always long for greater satisfaction and joy.

items.title: When God Is Against Me
items.summary: Can God act as a Christian’s enemy through suffering? Pastor John explains how God’s painful providences do not conflict with his enduring love for his children.

items.title: Can My Pain Kill My Sins?
items.summary: Does suffering kill the sin within us? Pastor John argues from 1 Peter 4:1 that believers die to sin with Christ so we can live to his righteousness.

items.title: Sex and the Romantic Solution (Open Forum)
items.summary: This talk was given by Dr. Timothy Keller at Redeemer Presbyterian Church on May 8, 2014. Series: Redeemer Open Forums. Today's podcast is brought to you by Gospel in Life, the site for all sermons, books, study guides and resources from Timothy Keller and Redeemer Presbyterian Church. If you've enjoyed listening to…

items.title: The Lions of God
items.summary: When we go out into the world as Christians, Jesus says our lives will have three characteristics. First, we are salt that preserves the people and societies around us from decay. Second, we will inevitably be hurt by those who misunderstand or reject our beliefs. Lastly, we will be like a light on a hill that…

items.title: The Finger on the Wall
items.summary: We all have a deep desire for our lives to have real significance. But when we try to find that fulfillment in romance, creativity, careers, or even religious obedience, we miss the only real solution there is: hope in Jesus Christ. Daniel shows us that when we trust in God’s Word, lay down our pride, and learn the…

items.title: The Man in the Furnace
items.summary: Many cultures today believe the idea that there are many moralities—and even many gods—that are all equally valid. Pluralism says that everyone is free to worship their god or way of life as long as they admit all of the others are just as real. But how can we as Christians maintain faith in one true God in a setting…

items.title: The Dream of the Kingdom
items.summary: After we become a Christian, there is a question that we inevitably ask ourselves: how do we live as a believer in an unbelieving world? Is it really possible to hold onto faith and integrity in a society that doesn’t operate on those values? Oftentimes we’re tempted to assimilate into our culture by leaving the…

items.title: Love and the Future of God
items.summary: We’ve been looking at the ways in which an experience of the grace of God creates a new interior character of the heart. At the end of 1 Corinthians 13, Paul tells us that the secret, the key, to developing that interior supernaturally changed heart is to look to the future—to something that’s going to happen in the…

items.title: Wholehearted Worship
items.summary: The Lord calls us to worship Him wholeheartedly every day of the week.

items.title: Grace to Keep Going
items.summary: God's grace doesn't end the moment we're saved. It's an ongoing reality that we can stand firm in.

items.title: Sufficient Grace
items.summary: Don't give up when the struggle comes. God sees the full picture when we can only see the pain.

items.title: A Commitment to Obey
items.summary: Obedience isn't a single moment of compliance; it's an unconditional surrender to following God.

items.title: The Passion to Obey
items.summary: As we grow in faith and dive deeper into His Word, our devotion to Him becomes stronger.

items.title: The Open Door
items.summary: Through hospitality, we turn our home and table into a ministry, reflecting the love of Christ.

items.title: New Every Morning
items.summary: The Lord's faithfulness, mercy, and love are available—today, tomorrow, and forever.

items.title: Faith, Perseverance & Prayer (2 Chronicles 35:22)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 35:22, David Platt reflects on the necessity of prayer for perseverance. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Pay Attention to God's Word (2 Chronicles 33:10)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 33:10, David Platt urges Christians to hear and obey God's Word. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Facing Opposition (2 Chronicles 32:7–8)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 32:7–8, David Platt teaches us how believers can face any challenge without fear. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Wholehearted Devotion (2 Chronicles 31:20–21)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 31:20–21, David Platt points us to wholehearted obedience flowing from love for God. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Living in Joy and Worship (2 Chronicles 30:23–27)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 30:23–27, David Platt emphasizes the believers’ identity as temples of the Holy Spirit today. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Returning to God (2 Chronicles 29:2)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 29:2, David Platt reminds Christians that a life honoring to God is filled with repentance. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Faithfulness in Times of Distress (2 Chronicles 28:22)
items.summary: In this episode of Pray the Word on 2 Chronicles 28:22, David Platt encourages believers to deepen their trust in God amid difficulties. Explore more content from Radical.

items.title: Nothing Is Hidden from God
items.summary: God doesn't just know about you. He knows you completely. His knowledge is perfect, personal, and without limitation. In this episode, Costi Hinn unpacks the omniscience of God and explains why being fully known by Him should change the way we live, pray, and respond to sin.

items.title: Nothing Happens Outside the Rule of God
items.summary: We often live as though everything depends on us, carrying the weight of circumstances we cannot control. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how understanding the sovereignty of God changes the way we approach uncertainty, suffering, and our daily lives. Resources: Earth's Epic Start: A Bible Study About God’s…

items.title: God’s Love Begins With Him, Not You
items.summary: God’s love is not something we earn through our obedience, nor is it an excuse to continue in sin. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how God’s love flows from His character, is revealed through Jesus Christ, and transforms how we love others. Resources: In Jesus' Name I Pray: TJ the Squirrel Learns the True Heart…

items.title: When God’s Glory Exposes Your Sin
items.summary: We are often quick to recognize the sins of others while overlooking our own. In this episode, Costi Hinn explains how seeing God in His holiness strips away our excuses, exposes our sin, and calls us to genuine repentance.

items.title: You Can Know God But Never Master Him
items.summary: In this episode, Costi Hinn explains what it means for God to be incomprehensible. God is infinitely greater than our minds can comprehend, yet He has made Himself truly knowable through His Word and ultimately through Jesus Christ.
